As a Scottish person (actually living in Scotland) I have access to both the NHS and several Chinese buffet establishments.

Not really a fan of a Chinese buffet to be honest, but if I pay my fee and feel a little peckish, I may return for another Spring Roll (think you call them egg rolls?) and some noodles.

I've yet to get the urge to just take a hatchet to my leg so that I can get a free prosthetic from the NHS.

I don't know all that much about your healthcare system. In some ways for those that can afford it, I'm sure it does well, better than ours actually. But dear god, how can you seriously begrudge someone being treated for a heart attack without bankrupting them.

An ambulance ride for instance. Over here, if you need an ambulance, you call 999 (our version of 911). We wait, all to recently these days, far too long admittedly), and one comes out with a couple of paramedics, loads you up and takes you to the hospital. In this country it costs us £0. Over in the US it from googling can cost up to $3500. What are the wages of those paramedics for the hour this process takes? What is the depreciation on the ambulance for this 1 ride? What are the overheads for the 911 call etc. I'm pretty sure that the cost will be actually closer to my £0 than to your $3500. Is it really a much more expensive endeavour than calling out someone to tow your car? Let's face it, paramedics ain't exactly coining it in like a footballer in terms of wages!

It's that middle layer in your system of these fucking Medical Insurance Companies that have to get their cut that are screwing you. In-house the bloody thing like other countries do and you will save yourselves a fucking fortune and people will be able to breathe a sigh of relief that they don't have to worry about choosing between treatment and their families house.

I say this not as some form of boasting foreigner. Our system is bursting at the seams too, with more privatisation and dodgy dealings from our politicians eroding what was once far better.

For us in the UK, we look to places like Germany and how they deal with envy now. It's not as socialist as us, but they seem to have a good balance.

When we look at what you guys have, we genuinely are horrified. You guys have a terrible system, and it can be so much better!
